# Prospective comparator challenge on held-out VitaminC pages

Earlier results on FEVER Symmetric and the first 128 VitaminC test pages in SHA-256 order are known. The full test file’s schema and aggregate label patterns were inspected for the prior transfer experiment. No example-level model outputs from the following test pages were used for design. Freeze the code and protocol hashes before test scoring. This is a retrospective public benchmark, with local prospective separation of the new cohort.

**Population.** Use only real revisions and the three released labels. Sort distinct Wikipedia page titles by the SHA-256 of their UTF-8 strings. Take pages at zero-based positions [128,256) of the official test release, including every row on those pages. Exclude every test-release page title from the official development release before selecting the first 192 remaining dev pages in hash order. If fewer independent dev pages exist, use all of them. Decisions and tuning operate on whole pages.

**Candidate.** Fit a regularized three-class multinomial logistic stack of the six published ALBERT base/xlarge checkpoint logits (VitaminC-only, +FEVER and +MNLI). Within each exact claim and revision case with two versions, augment each row with the other version's logits and their elementwise differences. A binary feature indicates partner availability. Pair context is drawn solely from the input batch. Choose regularization on dev pages, fit the meta-model on all eligible selected dev pages, and apply the fixed one-SUPPORTS rule to its scores. Use independent three-class predictions on nonpairs.

**Comparators.** Run each of the six published classifiers with ordinary argmax and with the same paired support-count decoder. Include unweighted logits averaged across all six checkpoints under both rules; independent and paired fitted row-only stacks; the context-aware stack without the support constraint. These controls separate the effects of extra weights, supervision and joint assignment. Retain all comparators and ties. Use identical IDs, candidate inputs, compute access and decision time. The published model training corpora differ across checkpoints. No claim against every possible verifier follows from this registry. The earlier BART/RoBERTa MNLI binary baselines belong to the separate FEVER Symmetric experiment. For the VitaminC transfer endpoint additionally compare each of those two evidence-aware systems with all three labels, independently and paired.

**Evaluation.** Fix C in {0.01, 0.1, 1} using three dev folds grouped by page. Minimize dev out-of-fold three-class log loss for the base meta-score, ties resolved in increasing C order. Standardize features within the fit fold. Primary endpoint is correctly classified rows at equal complete coverage, with 95% paired cluster intervals by page, 10,000 resamples and two-sided paired page sign-flips (20,000 Monte Carlo draws) with Holm across all declared contrasts. Require at least one percentage point observed gain and a positive interval lower endpoint and adjusted p < .05 against every eligible baseline. A tie or missing baseline keeps the paper outside the superiority count. Do not modify the method following test inspection. Save per-row decisions and per-page paired outcomes. Report separately the previously observed FEVER tie between unconstrained residualized logits and joint decoding.
